answers.answer: HTTPX is a Python HTTP client library with synchronous/asynchronous APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, pooling, cookies, authentication and streaming. Python applications import and call it; terminal users run the optional httpx CLI (project script httpx:main). Its own pytest tests also call the public API. No specific external downstream application inventory was established.

_api: convenience request functions. _client: shared configuration and synchronous/asynchronous request orchestration. _models: Request/Response, Headers/Cookies and body handling. _urls: URL/query representation and URL joining. _auth: authentication flows. _config: TLS, timeouts, connection limits and proxies. _transports: a pluggable request/response boundary; default transports adapt httpcore, ASGI/WSGI adapters call applications directly, and MockTransport calls a supplied handler. _main: optional terminal client.

Runtime and tests are Python; package metadata requires Python >=3.9. pyproject.toml uses the PEP 517 hatchling.build backend with hatchling and hatch-fancy-pypi-readme. This is one httpx distribution/import package, with internal modules and a _transports subpackage; tests are separate test code included in the sdist. httpcore, anyio, certifi and idna are external dependencies; CLI/HTTP2/SOCKS/compression are extras, not separate HTTPX services. Shell scripts drive pytest/coverage and Ruff; TOML configures mypy/pytest/Ruff, and Markdown supplies README/changelog packaging content.

Public httpx.get resolves through httpx/__init__.py's _api re-export and __all__. _api.get(url,...) calls _api.request('GET',url,...), which creates a context-managed Client and invokes client.request. The convenience call defaults follow_redirects=False; following must be requested explicitly.
BaseClient._redirect_method: 303/302 become GET except HEAD; 301 changes POST only; otherwise preserve the method, including 307/308.

Direct imports: _auth (Auth, BasicAuth, FunctionAuth); _models (Cookies, Headers, Request, Response); _transports.base (BaseTransport/AsyncBaseTransport); _transports.default (HTTPTransport/AsyncHTTPTransport). _utils.URLPattern supports dispatch.

Client.request→build_request→send→_build_request_auth→_send_handling_auth→_send_handling_redirects→_send_single_request→_transport_for_url→transport.handle_request. On has_redirect_location: _build_redirect_request→_redirect_method/_redirect_url/_redirect_headers/_redirect_stream→Request. Append history, read redirect response, repeat loop with rebuilt request; max_redirects bounds iteration. Dynamic boundaries: auth generators, request/response hooks, URL-dependent mounts and overridable transport.handle_request. Response.has_redirect_location requires status 301/302/303/307/308 plus Location, not merely any 3xx. Authentication can yield additional requests. The default HTTPTransport converts to httpcore.Request, invokes its pool, then wraps the returned response; the external networking implementation is outside this pinned repository. This is a static trace, not an observed network execution.

Direct consumer: BaseClient._build_redirect_request. Indirect effects: sync/async redirect loops, public methods, next_request, outgoing method and body/header preservation. Switching to GET drops the body and Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding. External subclass overrides remain dynamic. The POST/301 regression scenario enters through the public client API, not a direct call to _redirect_method.

tests/client/test_redirects.py::test_redirect_301 constructs Client(transport=MockTransport(redirects)) and calls client.post('https://example.org/redirect_301', follow_redirects=True). The redirects handler returns a 301 and Location=https://example.org/ for that path, then a synthetic 200 for the destination. MockTransport.handle_request reads the request and calls the Python handler directly, so no real network is needed. Assertions cover final OK status, destination URL and one history entry; this test exercises the method-rewrite branch but does not explicitly assert GET. I inspected, but did not run, the test.

At the default transport boundary, response headers arrive from httpcore and become Response.headers (Headers); the mock test instead supplies them directly. Headers lookup is case-insensitive. _redirect_url reads response.headers['Location']→URL(location); invalid parsing raises RemoteProtocolError. Repair scheme-without-host using prior host; join relative URLs; inherit prior fragment when absent; _build_redirect_request assigns the resulting URL. URL.join delegates to urllib.parse.urljoin and wraps the result as URL. The resulting URL is normalized again by Request construction.
